OVERVIEW

A gym member’s day, in one calm app

Who it is for

Gym members, regular and personal-training. The gym’s coach sets the plan; the member follows it.

What it does

Shows today’s workout and meals, logs them in seconds, turns results into visible progress.

What is underneath

A multi-programme platform. Gym today; a dietician or clinic can sit beside it, each with its own context.

Working prototype with sample data

Presenter note

The coach decides the plan; the app makes it easy to follow. Built to hold more than one programme, which matters in the next slide.

BEFORE / AFTER

One clear context at a time

The previous app home against the new one, on the three things that changed.

Navigation

BEFORE

Home / Health / Goals / Chat

→
AFTER

Today / Plans / Progress / [Provider]

Cards

BEFORE

Two programmes stacked on one screen

→
AFTER

Switch programme, one at a time

Data

BEFORE

Clinical readings mixed with gym logging

→
AFTER

Each belongs to its own programme

Presenter note

Real before-and-after. Old Home put blood pressure and sugar readings, gym attendance, and two programme cards (dietician plan, fitness plan), each with own trainer, goal and log button, in one long feed. Does not scale past two. New model: Instagram-style programme switcher; one programme’s context at a time and the whole app (nav, goal, data) changes with it. Every later decision follows from this.

STRUCTURE

Four tabs, one job each

Today

What to do now

Plans

What the coach set

Progress

How you are doing

Gym

The provider tab: membership, coach, assessments

Presenter note

Same four-slot navigation as before, but the last tab is the provider and changes with the active programme (Gym, Dietician, Clinic).

RESEARCH BASIS

Two sources, kept separate

VALIDATED

Real interviews with 3 to 4 gym trainers, one a head trainer. Only user-validated input behind the decisions.

SIMULATED

Proto-persona research used to fill gaps before real interviews were possible, shaped by the designer’s product judgment. Explicitly not user-tested.

Every pain point is tagged with its source. No usability scores, quotes or retention numbers exist yet; where a number would help we call it a hypothesis.

Presenter note

Trainer findings are from real interviews. Member findings behind the three headline decisions are simulated and not tested with members.

VALIDATED FINDINGSVALIDATED

What real trainers told us, and what we did about it

01
PAIN POINT

Regular members get a basic plan and little trainer attention compared with PT members

DECISION

Same plan system for everyone: AI-drafted, trainer-approved, editable by the member with the trainer notified

WHY

Regular members are not a lesser tier of the product

02
PAIN POINT

Trainers do not log workout or diet data for regular members

DECISION

Logging is member-driven for everyone, PT or not

WHY

The data exists whether or not a trainer is tracking it

03
PAIN POINT

One trainer covers about 30 members and cannot give 1:1 attention to each

DECISION

Self-service logging, assisted plans, async chat, contextual nudges

WHY

Less has to come from the trainer directly

04
PAIN POINT

Trainers focus on PT members’ assessments and progress

DECISION

Assessments and progress are the same for regular and PT members

WHY

Only trainer-chat direction and a few PT prompts differ

Presenter note

These four come from real trainer interviews. Caveat: AI-drafted plans is design intent; the prototype shows a coach-set plan.

THREE HEADLINE DECISIONSSIMULATED

Three decisions, one idea: keep members coming back

Each one starts from a member pain point and ends in something you can see in the prototype.

1

Something is better than nothing

Quick and Low-energy workouts, so a busy day does not mean a skipped session.

See decision 1 2

Train in the first session

A short guided setup, and the coach’s workout is on Today straight away.

See decision 2 3

Paused, not punished

Weekly streaks that pause instead of breaking, with a gentle way back.

See decision 3
DECISION 1 OF 3SIMULATED

Quick and Low-energy workouts: something is better than nothing

PROBLEM

Busy schedules make a full workout hard to keep up. People skip the session entirely rather than do a shorter one.

DECISION

Quick (20, 30 or 45 min) and Low-energy versions, chosen in the Start sheet. Both still count toward the streak.

WHY

A legitimate lighter path instead of all-or-nothing that ends in skipping.

Presenter note

Quick keeps the coach’s key exercises. Low energy keeps the same exercises, lighter. The choice lives only in the Start sheet so the Today card stays calm.

DECISION 1, CONTINUEDSIMULATED

Lighter sessions stay easy to run

One place to choose

Version is picked in the Start sheet only. Today card stays clean.

Fixed Next button, timer above it

Rest timer and Next button pinned at the bottom so the next action is always in reach.

Machine busy? Swap

Coach-approved alternatives, or search every exercise, for today only or for the plan.

Low-energy keeps the plan

Same exercises, lighter, so the member stays on the coach’s programme.

TO VALIDATE (HYPOTHESIS)

Share of sessions started as Quick or Low-energy, and how often sessions are skipped. Not measured.

DECISION 2 OF 3SIMULATED

Onboarding: get a new member training in their first session

PROBLEM

First visit is awkward: nothing to do while the trainer prepares a plan, and too many unrelated setup questions up front.

DECISION

Short guided setup: goal, experience, schedule, then body and consent. The coach’s workout is on Today straight away.

WHY

A new member can train in the first session instead of waiting on a plan.

Presenter note

Progress bar 1 of 7 (1 of 8 when a weight target is needed). Starts with a welcome from gym and coach; body details use tactile rulers; consent and privacy last.

DECISION 3 OF 3SIMULATED

Streaks that pause instead of punishing

PROBLEM

Missed days create guilt and shame; a broken streak is a classic reason people drop out of fitness apps.

DECISION

Weekly streak of 4 sessions. Framed as “paused, not lost”, no blame wording, gentle comeback.

WHY

Keeps the habit pull of a streak without the drop-off a broken streak causes.

Presenter note

Weeks not days; one rest pass a month applied automatically; membership pause freezes the streak; misses are neutral grey, never red; lighter sessions count.

DECISION 3, CONTINUEDSIMULATED

Coming back after a gap feels welcoming

“Streak paused, not lost”

After a break Today offers a 30-minute restart session, not a lecture.

Weekly, not daily

Four sessions a week. One missed day never breaks anything.

A rest pass each month

If a week is missed, a pass keeps the streak, applied automatically.

Calm history

12-week strip shows a missed week in neutral grey, no red.

TO VALIDATE (HYPOTHESIS)

Whether members return after a gap more often with this flow. Not measured.

SUPPORTING PAIN POINTSSIMULATED

Smaller decisions that support the three above

SUPPORTING PAIN POINTSSIMULATED

Plans and food that fit how people really train and eat

Indian food, in Indian units

Roti, katori, bowl instead of grams and macro-first logging, with nutritional-equivalent swaps.

Experienced lifters are not boxed in

Experience-level question and full edit rights on any plan; no separate restrictive mode.

Real numbers stay real

Warm-up sets logged separately so they do not distort true numbers. (Design intent, not shown in prototype.)

One amount control

Direct minus and plus on each food; 2 roti to 3 takes one tap.

SUPPORTING PAIN POINTSSIMULATED

Several providers, each in its own space

Programme switcher

Gym, dietician, clinic feel connected but stay separate; one programme’s goal, plan and data at a time.

Consent-based data silos

Each programme only sees what the member allows, with a privacy page per provider.

Goals per programme

Progress adapts to the member’s actual goal in that programme.

Photos private by default

Members are uncomfortable with a trainer seeing progress photos, so only the member sees them.

Presenter note

The progress photo shown is a stand-in of a real person. Replace with licensed content before any wider use.

SUPPORTING PAIN POINTSSIMULATED

Trust and access, handled quietly

PT sessions need two signatures

Trainer marks session complete; member confirms and rates it. Ratings visible to gym admin only, never to the trainer.

No sudden lockout

At membership expiry a grace period keeps history and logging open; after it, history stays visible.

Membership is view-only

Pauses and payments handled by the front desk. App shows history and pauses left.

FOR PT MEMBERS

Built for personal-training members too

Regular and PT members share one app. These points apply only to members with a PT pack.

1

Packs set by the gym

The gym admin creates a PT pack: a session count and a validity period. No fixed duration, and nothing to pre-book.

2

Invite, then accept

The trainer sends the invite. The member accepts or rejects it directly before any session runs.

3

Two signatures per session

The trainer marks a session complete. The member confirms it and adds remarks.

4

A rating after each session

Ratings roll up to an overall trainer score. Only the gym admin sees it, never the trainer.

5

Assessments you can add to

Trainer assessments stay official. Members can log their own readings in between, tagged by source, without replacing the next reassessment.

6

A direction from the trainer

Trainer chat and a few PT prompts are specific to PT members. The plan, logging and progress are the same as for everyone.

REGULAR MEMBER

Attendance is marked by the member: check-in, QR or biometric.

PT MEMBER

Sessions are marked by the trainer and confirmed by the member.

KNOWN GAP

Women’s representation: deliberately deferred

WHAT CAME UP

Early research raised women’s representation, e.g. female trainer demonstrations.

WHAT WE DID

Scoped out of this version on purpose. Not solved here and not claimed to be.

WHAT IT NEEDS

Scoped properly with the gym team and tested, not patched in late.

Presenting this as a scoping decision, not an oversight.

Presenter note

Name it openly; candidate for next phase.

FUTURE SCOPEIDEA

Where this could go next

Three ideas, shown as concept sketches. None of these are built, and none are tested with members.

FOOD

Order from Swiggy

The diet plan already says what to eat. This lets a member order a matching meal when they do not want to cook.

  1. 1Plan shows today’s lunch
  2. 2App lists matching meals nearby
  3. 3Order completes in Swiggy

Needs a partner integration. Not confirmed.

FOOD

Ingredients from Blinkit

For members who cook at home, the week’s plan becomes a grocery list they can send to a basket.

  1. 1Plan builds the week’s ingredient list
  2. 2Member ticks what they already have
  3. 3Basket opens in Blinkit

Needs a partner integration. Not confirmed.

COMMUNITY

Community wall and wall of fame

One shared space for the gym. Trainers and members post workouts and achievements, and milestones are pinned to a wall of fame.

  1. 1Trainers and members post a workout or an achievement
  2. 2Milestones such as streaks and goals reached are pinned to the wall of fame
  3. 3Members choose whether they appear

Posting is opt-in. Progress photos stay private by default, as in the current design.

Presenter note

Two directions: food, by connecting the diet plan to ordering and groceries; and community, by letting members and trainers share progress and celebrate milestones. Food needs partner access to be agreed first. Community needs moderation and clear opt-in.

WHAT’S NEXT

Test the decisions with real members

1

Validate

Three hypotheses not yet measured: Quick/Low-energy reduce skipped sessions; short onboarding gets members to a first session; “paused, not lost” brings members back after a gap.

2

Build

Backend for accounts, real codes and plans; connected health data; coach and owner dashboard.

3

Pilot

One gym, one coach; replace stand-in photos with licensed content.

Honest status: working prototype with sample data, no backend. Thank you.
